column1: # DISCLOSURE GUARD — EXAMPLE rules file.
# Copy to `private/disclosure-denylist.tsv` (gitignored) and fill in the terms that
# would disclose YOUR deployments. This example names nobody, on purpose: a denylist
# that spells a customer's name discloses that customer, and a public repo is the
# last place it belongs. Mechanism public, vocabulary private — the same narrow waist
# the engine itself is built on.
#   cp tools/disclosure-denylist.example.tsv private/disclosure-denylist.tsv
#   ln -sf ../../tools/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit
#   tools/disclosure_guard.py --selftest
# FORMAT, TAB-SEPARATED:   pattern <TAB> control <TAB> why [<TAB> name]
#   pattern  a Python regex, matched case-insensitively.
#   control  ⭐ a string the pattern MUST match. Refused at load time if it does not.
#            This is what makes a green `--selftest` mean "the matcher ran" instead of
#            "nothing was checked". You cannot add a rule without its evidence.
#   why      printed on a hit. Name the RIGHT FIX. An author told only "denied string"
#            deletes the word — the wrong repair when the real one is to move the test
#            into private/tests/ or take the domain back out of the engine.
#   name     optional short id for the output.
# ⛔ WHAT NO DENYLIST CAN DO. It catches only what somebody thought to add. A client
#    named for the first time tomorrow, a project codename, an internal hostname, or a
#    fixture full of one customer's distinctive jargon all pass untouched. Structural
#    rules (absolute home paths) are built into the tool because they name nobody and
#    are therefore safe to publish; identity rules belong here.
# ⛔ NOTE the domain used below is `exampleco.ds`, NOT `acme.ds`. `acme.ds` is the
#    SYNTHETIC domain the public test suite uses as the approved replacement, and the
#    guard carries it as a NEGATIVE control. A rule denying it would make the guard
#    forbid its own remedy — and a gate that fires on the fix gets switched off.
examplecorp
column3: a customer's name. It belongs in no public artifact of this repo.

column1: exampledata
column3: a customer's data root. Live-corpus tests belong in the gitignored private/tests/ overlay, not in tests/.

column1: \bexampleco\.ds\b
column3: a real domain id. The engine loads domain vocabulary from a PROFILE at runtime, so an id in engine source is a fork across that seam. Use a synthetic domain with the same SHAPE.
